items.name: Import or Export Watch State Manually
items.description: Runs a one-off Import or Export against a watch-sync provider for one user.

fields.label: Primary Source
fields.description: First enrichment source to try

fields.label: Fallback Source
fields.description: Second source if primary misses fields. Set to None to disable. Discogs needs a token — add it under Settings → Plugins → Discogs.

fields.label: Primary Source
fields.description: First enrichment source to try

fields.label: Fallback Source
fields.description: Second source if primary misses fields. Set to None to disable. Discogs needs a token — add it under Settings → Plugins → Discogs.

fields.label: Third Source
fields.description: Third source if the first two miss. Set to None to disable. Deezer is keyless and has by far the best coverage of obscure artists, so it is the default here.

fields.label: Provider
fields.description: Which popularity provider to use. More providers will be added in future releases.

fields.label: Last.fm API Key
fields.description: API key from last.fm/api/account/create. Free; required when source is Last.fm.

fields.label: Refresh Interval (days)
fields.description: An artist is considered stale — and re-fetched on the next drain — once its popularity row is older than this many days. Default 7.

fields.label: Data URL
fields.description: URL to the anime-list-full.json file. Useful for pointing at a local mirror or a pinned commit. Leave empty to use the official Fribb GitHub source.

items.name: Detect Intros & Credits
items.description: Detects intro / outro / recap / preview / commercial segments in episodes via FFmpeg fingerprint + chromaprint matching. Results power skip buttons in the player. Tune throughput with the batchSize and episodeConcurrency settings.

fields.label: Chapter name detection
fields.description: Detect segments from embedded chapter metadata (no FFmpeg needed)

fields.label: Black frame credits detection
fields.description: Detect credits via black frame analysis (requires FFmpeg)

fields.label: Audio fingerprint intro detection
fields.description: Detect intros by comparing audio across episodes in a season (requires FFmpeg with chromaprint)

fields.label: Seasons per scheduled run
fields.description: How many seasons one scheduled run analyses. Raise it to finish a large library sooner; lower it on a small or busy server.

fields.label: Episode concurrency
fields.description: Episodes analysed at the same time. Higher is faster but uses more CPU; lower it on a small server.

fields.label: FFmpeg threads per operation
fields.description: CPU threads each FFmpeg process may use (0 = let FFmpeg decide).

fields.label: Max intro duration (seconds)
fields.description: Longest intro that will be accepted.

fields.label: Credits search window (seconds)
fields.description: How far before the end of an episode to look for closing credits. This only widens the search — the longest credits that are accepted is set separately below.

fields.label: Movie credits search window (seconds)
fields.description: The same search window for movies, whose credits run longer.

fields.label: Max plausible credits length, episodes (seconds)
fields.description: Longest closing credits an episode may have; a longer detection is discarded.

fields.label: Max plausible credits length, movies (seconds)
fields.description: Longest closing credits a movie may have; a longer detection is discarded.

fields.label: Minimum credits start position (0–1)
fields.description: How far into an episode the credits must start. 0.80 means anything that starts before 80 % of the runtime is not treated as credits. Not applied to movies.

fields.label: Chapter snap tolerance (seconds)
fields.description: How far a detected start or end may move to line up with a chapter mark in the file. 0 turns this off.

fields.label: Audio match tolerance
fields.description: How different two audio fingerprints may be and still count as the same intro. Lower is stricter; raise it only if intros are being missed.

fields.label: Audio match gap (seconds)
fields.description: Largest gap between matching audio moments before a match counts as broken.

fields.label: Intro search window (share of episode, 0–1)
fields.description: How much of each episode, from the start, is searched for the intro. 0.25 = the first quarter.

fields.label: Intro search window limit (seconds)
fields.description: Upper limit on that search window.

fields.label: Audio index tolerance
fields.description: How loosely the audio search index matches. Higher finds more candidates but is slower.

fields.label: Shortest segment (seconds)
fields.description: Ignore detected intros or credits shorter than this.

fields.label: Anime: mark a preview after the credits
fields.description: After the credits, mark what remains of the episode (at least 5 seconds) as a Preview, as anime episodes often end with one. It is not detected automatically — turn it on only if your library is mostly anime.
